name: Wounded Warrior Project
story: Every **{mental-health: cost_total / (people_reached + opt_veterans + opt_family + cns_people)|$}** gives one veteran or family member mental health treatment, and every **{other-programmes: cost_total / (ben_people + people_reached + emp_placed * household_size)|$}** helps one household with benefits, jobs or money.
summary: A US charity for veterans injured in military service since 11 September 2001 and their families: mental health care through four academic medical centres, help winning VA disability benefits, job placement, social and fitness programmes, long-term care for the most severely injured, grants to other veteran charities and lobbying in Washington.

spending.source: https://www.woundedwarriorproject.org/media/fbopl3fq/fy2025-wounded-warrior-project-form-990.pdf (Form 990 for the year to 30 September 2025: programme service expenses $274,648,975; the audited statements' $339.9M adds $63.8M of donated public service announcements at the media's rate card and other in-kind items, which no donor pays for)

lines.label: Mental health: Warrior Care Network's intensive PTSD programmes, therapy, counselling, Project Odyssey, WWP Talk
lines.source: https://www.woundedwarriorproject.org/media/fbopl3fq/fy2025-wounded-warrior-project-form-990.pdf (Schedule O, Part III line 4a: mental health programmes $98,748,548, including $35,419,052 of grants to Warrior Care Network)

lines.label: Benefits, jobs, financial help, connection, physical health, the Independence Program, community partnerships and advocacy
lines.source: https://www.woundedwarriorproject.org/media/fbopl3fq/fy2025-wounded-warrior-project-form-990.pdf (Schedule O, Part III lines 4b-4d: independence $47,390,694, connection $42,763,171, financial wellness $38,821,354, physical health $21,175,587, community partnerships $19,615,919, government relations $6,133,702)
